sentence: A well-structured page starts with <!DOCTYPE html> followed by <html lang="en"> as the root, then a <head> containing metadata like <meta charset="utf-8"> and <title>Page</title>, and finally a <body> for visible content. Semantic regions such as <header>, <main>, <nav>, and <footer> communicate page structure to assistive technology and search engines in ways that generic <div> wrappers cannot.

Article-style content benefits from wrapping each post in an <article> element, with its title in an <h2> or <h3> and metadata such as the publication date inside a <time datetime="2024-09-12">12 September 2024</time>. The machine-readable datetime attribute lets parsers extract the date without depending on the localised text rendered in the document.

Inline annotations frequently use <abbr title="HyperText Markup Language">HTML</abbr> for abbreviations and <dfn>defining instance</dfn> when introducing a term. For citations to external sources, <cite>The Elements of Typographic Style</cite> displays a work title in italics by default while preserving the semantic meaning that screen readers and bibliographic tools can act on.

Headings should descend in document order without skipping levels, so an <h1> is followed by <h2> rather than jumping to <h4>. Tools like Lighthouse and axe report skipped heading levels as accessibility violations because users navigating with the heading shortcuts of NVDA or VoiceOver depend on a coherent outline.

Inline phrasing uses for strong importance and for stress emphasis, both of which are semantically distinct from purely presentational and . Modern usage prefers wrapping a foreign-language term in déjà vu so that the italic styling is paired with a lang attribute that a screen reader can use to switch pronunciation.

The <head> typically also contains <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"> so mobile browsers treat the viewport as the device's actual width rather than the legacy 980-pixel default. Without that meta the page will render at desktop width and shrink to fit, producing tiny illegible text on phones.

and the URL placed in the cite attribute is intended for machine consumption rather than display. Visible source attribution should follow the quote in a

Pages with multiple navigation regions should distinguish them with aria-label, for example <nav aria-label="Primary"> for the top menu and <nav aria-label="Breadcrumb"> for breadcrumbs. The label becomes part of the accessible name presented when a screen-reader user lists landmarks, and reduces the ambiguity of multiple unnamed <nav> elements on the page.

Every form control needs an associated label. The simplest pattern is <label for="email">Email</label><input id="email" type="email" name="email" required>, which ties the label text to the input by matching id and for. Wrapping the input inside the label also works and removes the need for the id altogether.

Client-side validation can be declared directly on the element. <input type="number" min="1" max="100" step="1" required> rejects empty submissions and out-of-range values before the form is sent, and the browser surfaces a native error tooltip in the user's language. The pattern attribute accepts a regex, as in pattern="[A-Z]{3}-\d{4}" for a structured reference number.

Grouping related controls in <fieldset> with a <legend> at the top gives screen-reader users the context they need before encountering each input. A typical pattern is <fieldset><legend>Shipping address</legend>...inputs...</fieldset>, which the browser also styles with a thin border by default.

The <select> element with a series of <option> children produces a native dropdown that on mobile typically opens the platform's wheel picker. For long lists, <optgroup label="Europe"> can subdivide the options into labelled groups: <select><optgroup label="Europe"><option>France</option><option>Germany</option></optgroup></select>.

Skip links let keyboard users jump past repetitive navigation. The pattern is to place Skip to main content as the first focusable element on the page and use CSS to keep it visually hidden until it receives focus, so that mouse users do not see it but keyboard users encounter it on the first Tab press.

Inputs that show search suggestions can use <input list="countries"><datalist id="countries"><option value="France"><option value="Germany"></datalist>, which produces a free-text field with autocomplete pulled from the datalist. The browser handles the suggestion UI and keyboard navigation without any JavaScript.

Error messages should be programmatically associated with their input using aria-describedby. At least 12 characters, one symbol. ensures that when a screen reader focuses the password field the helper text is announced along with the label.

The autocomplete attribute is more than a convenience: setting <input type="text" name="cc-number" autocomplete="cc-number"> on credit-card fields lets password managers and platform autofill recognise and supply the right value, and is required by recent WCAG criteria for inputs that collect personal data.

Radio groups share a single name attribute so that selecting one deselects the others: <input type="radio" name="size" value="s" id="s"><label for="s">Small</label><input type="radio" name="size" value="m" id="m"><label for="m">Medium</label>. Checkbox groups use distinct names because each captures an independent boolean.

Submission targets can be overridden per-button. A form may have <button type="submit" formaction="/save-draft">Save draft</button> and <button type="submit" formaction="/publish">Publish</button> side by side, sending the same payload to two different endpoints depending on which button the user pressed.

Data tables benefit from explicit row and column headers. A pattern like

lets screen readers announce both the column and row context when reading a cell.

A short <caption>Annual revenue by region, 2020-2024</caption> immediately after the <table> opening tag is announced before the table content and gives users an overview before they navigate the cells. Captions render above the table by default but their position is adjustable with CSS caption-side.

Description lists pair terms with descriptions: <dl><dt>HTML</dt><dd>The markup language used to structure web pages.</dd><dt>CSS</dt><dd>A style-sheet language used to describe presentation.</dd></dl>. They are appropriate for glossaries, metadata, and key-value pairings where an ordered or unordered list would be semantically wrong.
Images intended as content require alternative text. communicates the substantive information of the image to users who cannot see it. Purely decorative images take an empty alt: .
Responsive images can use . The browser walks the source elements in order and selects the first match, falling back to the inner img if none apply.

Video and audio can be embedded natively with <video controls width="640" poster="thumb.jpg"><source src="lecture.webm" type="video/webm"><source src="lecture.mp4" type="video/mp4"><track kind="captions" src="lecture.en.vtt" srclang="en" label="English"></video>. The <track> element supplies captions or subtitles in a WebVTT file.

Lazy-loading images is a single-attribute change: . The width and height attributes are important even when CSS controls the displayed size, because they let the browser reserve layout space and avoid cumulative layout shift.

Long content that wraps over multiple rows or columns uses rowspan and colspan: Total merges two columns in a row, and Q1 spans three rows of a row-group. Overuse of span attributes makes tables hard to read with assistive technology and should be confined to genuine grouping.
Figures with captions use . The

External content can be embedded with <iframe src="https://example.org/widget" title="Live exchange rates" loading="lazy" referrerpolicy="no-referrer" sandbox="allow-scripts"></iframe>. The title is required for accessibility, and the sandbox attribute restricts what the embedded document can do, defaulting to an empty allow-list when present without a value.

sentence: Linking a stylesheet uses <link rel="stylesheet" href="/styles/main.css"> in the document head. For non-critical styles, the same tag with media="print" or media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" lets the browser download the file but defer applying it until the matching condition is met, reducing render-blocking on the critical path.

subtopic: CSS integration via class and style
sentence: Component classes can be combined on a single element: <button class="btn btn--primary btn--lg">Continue</button>. Each class contributes a single concern, so the .btn class supplies the base typography and box model, .btn--primary applies the brand colour, and .btn--lg adjusts the padding for a larger size.

The remaining styles are linked normally, and the inline block avoids a render-blocking round-trip for the first painted frame.

sentence: Print stylesheets benefit from semantic markup. Adding <link rel="stylesheet" href="/styles/print.css" media="print"> pairs the page with a sheet that hides <nav> and <aside>, sizes <article> body text for paper, and uses a::after to append each link's href after its visible label so the printout remains usable offline. Such media-targeted stylesheets do not block initial render.

sentence: Light- and dark-mode support can be expressed entirely declaratively. Setting <meta name="color-scheme" content="light dark"> and writing CSS with :root { --bg: white } and @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { :root { --bg: #111 } } makes the user agent honour the OS preference for form controls, scrollbars, and your own custom colours alike.

A standard card grid combines markup and modern CSS layout. <section class="grid"><article class="card">...</article><article class="card">...</article></section> paired with .grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(16rem, 1fr)); gap: 1rem } produces a responsive layout that adapts to any viewport width without media queries.

opens above other content, dismisses on outside click or Escape, and requires no script for the common cases.

Scalable vector graphics can be inlined directly. <svg viewBox="0 0 100 100" role="img" aria-label="Logo"><circle cx="50" cy="50" r="40" fill="currentColor"/></svg> uses currentColor so the icon picks up the surrounding text colour automatically, which is useful for theme switching and for ensuring that focus styles propagate consistently.

Custom elements register a new tag that the browser treats as a real component. After class definition and customElements.define("like-button", LikeButton), markup like <like-button count="42" data-target="post-71"></like-button> participates in normal HTML parsing while delegating its behaviour and shadow DOM to the JavaScript class.

Lazy script loading uses the type and async attributes carefully. <script src="/app.js" type="module" async></script> instructs the browser to fetch the module without blocking parsing and to execute it as soon as it is ready, an order independent of other scripts and suitable for an entry point that does not depend on inline code.

Open Graph metadata governs how a URL appears when shared on social platforms. Tags like <meta property="og:title" content="Annual Report 2024">, <meta property="og:image" content="https://example.org/og.jpg">, and <meta property="og:description" content="How we performed against our 2024 goals."> become a card preview rather than a bare link.

A two-column shell with sticky sidebar is concise with modern CSS. <body class="layout"><nav class="layout__side">...</nav><main class="layout__main">...</main></body> plus .layout { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 16rem 1fr } and .layout__side { position: sticky; top: 0; height: 100vh } gives a navigation rail that stays visible while the main column scrolls.

Hidden but accessible content is a recurring need. The pattern Sale ends Friday paired with .sr-only { position: absolute; width: 1px; height: 1px; overflow: hidden; clip: rect(0 0 0 0); white-space: nowrap } removes the text from the visual flow without hiding it from screen readers or breaking selection in assistive tooling.

subtopic: CSS integration via class and style
sentence: Conditional class application from JavaScript uses the classList API rather than overwriting className. Given markup like <button class="toggle">Menu</button>, calling document.querySelector(".toggle").classList.toggle("is-active") flips the class on and off without disturbing other classes already on the element, which is essential when several scripts cooperate to style the same component.

Sandboxed iframes restrict what embedded content can do. The pattern <iframe src="https://untrusted.example.org/widget" sandbox="allow-scripts allow-same-origin" loading="lazy" title="Widget"></iframe> permits scripts and same-origin access while denying form submission, top-level navigation, and pointer lock by default. Each capability must be re-granted explicitly through the sandbox token list.

The allow attribute on an iframe controls feature-policy permissions for the embedded document. A video conferencing widget might use <iframe src="/meet" allow="camera; microphone; display-capture; clipboard-read" title="Live meeting"></iframe> to grant the embedded origin access to hardware that ordinary iframes cannot use.

YouTube and other media providers expose privacy-respecting embed URLs that suppress cookies until playback. The markup <iframe width="560" height="315" src="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/dQw4w9WgXcQ" title="Video" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture" allowfullscreen></iframe> embeds a player with reduced tracking and the full set of fullscreen and orientation capabilities.

The referrerpolicy attribute on an iframe constrains what Referer header is sent with the embedded document's outgoing requests. Setting <iframe src="https://maps.example.com/embed" referrerpolicy="no-referrer-when-downgrade" loading="lazy" title="Map"></iframe> matches the document's normal policy and prevents leakage when downgrading from HTTPS to HTTP.

An <embed> element supplies a generic mechanism for plug-in or media content. The form <embed src="document.pdf" type="application/pdf" width="100%" height="600"> instructs the browser to render the resource using its registered handler for the supplied MIME type, falling back to a download offer if no handler exists. The older <object> element provides similar functionality with nested fallback content.

Posting messages between an iframe and its embedder requires window.postMessage and a deliberate origin check. The parent uses a snippet like document.querySelector('iframe').contentWindow.postMessage({type:'theme',value:'dark'},'https://child.example.org') while the iframe receives via window.addEventListener('message', e => { if (e.origin !== 'https://parent.example.org') return; }), and the HTML host needs only the original <iframe id="app" src="https://child.example.org" title="App"></iframe> for the channel to exist.

Iframe resizing across origins typically depends on cooperative scripting because the parent cannot read the child's scroll height directly. A common pattern is the child posting its dimensions on resize: <iframe id="widget" src="https://widget.example.org" style="width:100%;border:0" title="Widget"></iframe> in the parent, with a content script that watches its document height and sends it up to be applied to iframe.style.height.

OAuth flows often use a popup or a redirected iframe to complete consent. A login button might trigger a separate window rather than embedding the identity provider directly, since most authentication services refuse to be framed and indicate this through an X-Frame-Options: DENY response header. A typical markup remnant is <button id="login" type="button" data-provider="google">Sign in with Google</button> that opens a tab rather than embedding the provider page.

The csp attribute on iframes enables an embedded Content Security Policy that must be respected by the embedded document. The pattern <iframe csp="script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'" src="/widget.html" title="Widget"></iframe> hardens the embedding boundary against compromised partial-trust content. Compatibility is still uneven and a Content-Security-Policy response header is usually a more reliable defence.

Embedding maps from a third party usually involves an iframe with carefully fixed dimensions. The classic snippet <iframe src="https://www.openstreetmap.org/export/embed.html?bbox=-0.2%2C51.4%2C0.0%2C51.6&layer=mapnik" width="600" height="400" style="border:1px solid #ccc" title="Map of central London" loading="lazy"></iframe> embeds a static map view with a bounding box query string and lazy loading to defer the network request until scroll.

Custom elements register tags that participate in the DOM like any built-in element. After class CounterElement extends HTMLElement {} is registered with customElements.define('counter-widget', CounterElement), the markup <counter-widget value="0" step="1"></counter-widget> instantiates the component anywhere in the document with a hyphenated name that guarantees forward compatibility with future built-in elements.

The slot mechanism allows a custom element to declare insertion points in its shadow DOM that the host fills with light DOM content. A definition like

Customised built-in elements extend an existing tag rather than creating a new one. Registering class FancyButton extends HTMLButtonElement {} with customElements.define('fancy-button', FancyButton, { extends: 'button' }) is invoked in markup as <button is="fancy-button" type="submit">Buy</button>, preserving the host element's accessibility semantics and form integration while overlaying new behaviour.

Form-associated custom elements participate in the surrounding form by declaring static formAssociated = true. The host markup <user-form><name-input name="first" required></name-input><name-input name="last" required></name-input><button type="submit">Save</button></user-form> submits values from the custom inputs as if they were native inputs, provided each custom element calls this.internals_.setFormValue() in its connected callback.

Declarative shadow DOM removes the need for JavaScript to attach a shadow root for static content. The fragment Hello

Lifecycle callbacks let a custom element react to insertion, removal, and attribute changes. A class with connectedCallback(), disconnectedCallback(), attributeChangedCallback(name, oldVal, newVal), and a static observedAttributes getter returning ['theme', 'value'] is paired with markup like <toggle-button theme="dark" value="off"></toggle-button> so that attribute updates propagate immediately into the shadow tree.

The :host and :host-context pseudo-classes style the custom element from inside its shadow tree. Inside a component's <style> block, :host { display: contents } removes the element from layout while leaving its slotted children visible, and :host([disabled]) { opacity: 0.5 } responds to the host element's own attributes in markup such as <icon-button disabled label="Send"></icon-button>.

Custom events flow up through composedPath when they cross shadow boundaries. A definition like this.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('toggle', { bubbles: true, composed: true, detail: { open: true } })) ensures that markup higher up such as <accordion-group><accordion-panel></accordion-panel></accordion-group> can register a single listener on the group and observe events from each panel without piercing the shadow tree.

Lazy component registration avoids loading bundles until the relevant tag actually appears. The markup <product-quickview product-id="sku-1234"></product-quickview> can be hydrated by an IntersectionObserver that imports the component module only when the element enters the viewport, with the unupgraded tag rendering whatever default content the slot provides until then.

The :defined pseudo-class targets custom elements that have already been registered. A page can hide unupgraded markup with a stylesheet rule like :not(:defined) { visibility: hidden } applied to elements such as <hero-banner></hero-banner> and <pricing-grid columns="3"></pricing-grid>, which avoids the brief unstyled flash while the JavaScript bundle that defines them is still loading.

Data attributes are author-defined hooks of the form data-* that the platform exposes to JavaScript through the element's dataset property. Markup like <article data-published="2024-08-15" data-author-id="42" data-tags="news,policy"></article> is read as article.dataset.published and article.dataset.authorId, with hyphenated names converted to camelCase automatically.

CSS attribute selectors give data attributes presentational power without classes. A rule like [data-state="loading"] .spinner { display: inline } applies whenever markup such as updates a single attribute, with the rest of the styling cascade unaffected.

Test automation frameworks frequently reserve a dedicated data- attribute for selector stability. The pattern <button class="btn btn--primary" data-testid="checkout-submit" type="submit">Place order</button> survives refactoring of class names and copy changes, and many style guides recommend that test selectors never use visually meaningful classes or text content.

Counters and badges can be rendered entirely through CSS using data attributes. With a rule like .nav-item[data-count]::after { content: attr(data-count); background: red; color: white; border-radius: 99px; padding: 0 0.4em }, the markup Inbox shows a count badge that vanishes whenever the attribute is removed by the application.

Templating libraries often store reactive state in data- prefixes on the root element. Alpine.js, for example, parses

where the x- attributes are custom directives processed by the framework at runtime without browser-level support but valid as authoring syntax.

Internationalisation can be driven through data attributes that key into a translation table. A pattern like

Welcome

with a script that walks document.querySelectorAll('[data-i18n]') and replaces text content with translations[el.dataset.i18n] is a common minimum viable approach that does not require a full framework or build step.

Analytics tracking is frequently encoded as a small grammar of data attributes the page reads on click. The element Pricing can be captured by a single delegated listener that reads dataset.analyticsEvent and pushes a normalised payload to the analytics queue.

Sortable tables sometimes encode parsed values in data attributes so that sorting does not need to re-parse cell text. A row like 31 Jul 2024$43.99 lets a sorting routine compare the numeric data-sort values directly while preserving the display formatting of the visible cell contents.

Drag-and-drop reordering benefits from stable data-* identifiers on each draggable. The pattern

Feature flagging can be expressed on the document root and inherited by descendant selectors. Setting <html data-feature-new-checkout="true" data-feature-dark-launch="control"> at server-render time allows stylesheet rules like html[data-feature-new-checkout="true"] .legacy-checkout { display: none } to control visibility without touching individual elements at runtime.

Live regions inform assistive technologies that a dynamic part of the page may update with information the user has not requested. The pattern
Cart updated: 3 items
announces changes to screen readers without interrupting the current speech, and aria-live="assertive" elevates the urgency for critical alerts.

pairs each tab with its panel and broadcasts the selection state.

The aria-expanded attribute communicates the open or closed state of a disclosure to screen readers. Markup like

conveys the collapsed state to assistive tech and is toggled with the matching hidden attribute on the menu.

Landmark roles let assistive-technology users skip between major page regions. A page wraps its top-level structure in <header role="banner"><nav role="navigation" aria-label="Primary">...</nav></header><main role="main">...</main><aside role="complementary" aria-label="Related links">...</aside><footer role="contentinfo">...</footer>, although in modern HTML the elements themselves carry these roles implicitly and explicit role attributes are mostly redundant.

Decorative icons should be hidden from assistive technologies while functional icons need accessible labels. The contrast appears in for a purely decorative chevron and for the close button where the only label is the icon itself.

A combobox pattern combines an input with a listbox popup and demands a careful tower of ARIA attributes. The pattern
  • Sydney
coordinates focus, selection, and announcement in a way no single attribute can.

The accessible name of an element is computed through a precise algorithm and aria-label overrides the inner text. A button rendered as <button aria-label="Add to favourites"><svg aria-hidden="true" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path d="M12 4l3 6 6 1-5 4 1 7-5-3-5 3 1-7-5-4 6-1z"/></svg></button> exposes the label to assistive tech regardless of the visible SVG glyph, and aria-labelledby would point to an element whose text constitutes the name.

Progress and status conveyance is split between several patterns. A loading indicator that no user explicitly invoked uses
Loading results
, while a determinate progress bar takes 60%, and an indeterminate spinner pairs an animated visual with Loading, please wait announced to screen readers only.

The role="presentation" and role="none" attributes strip an element of its implicit semantics. A purely layout table can use
LogoTagline
so screen readers do not announce row and column structure that has no semantic meaning, although modern practice strongly discourages layout tables in favour of grid and flexbox CSS.

JSON-LD is the most commonly recommended structured-data format for search-engine consumption. A typical product page embeds a <script type="application/ld+json">{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"Product","name":"Widget X","sku":"WX-001","offers":{"@type":"Offer","price":"29.99","priceCurrency":"USD","availability":"https://schema.org/InStock"}}</script> block in the head, decoupled from the visible markup yet read by crawlers.

Recipe sites compete fiercely for the rich-result treatment by encoding their structure carefully. The pattern <script type="application/ld+json">{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"Recipe","name":"Sourdough loaf","recipeIngredient":["500g bread flour","350g water","10g salt"],"cookTime":"PT40M","recipeYield":"1 loaf"}</script> places ingredients in a list and the cooking duration in ISO 8601 duration form for automated parsing.

Article pages benefit from explicit author and publication date metadata. A news article carries <script type="application/ld+json">{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"NewsArticle","headline":"Election result certified","datePublished":"2025-11-08T14:23:00+11:00","author":{"@type":"Person","name":"S. Lin"},"publisher":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Example News"}}</script>, which can drive both rich results and CMS exports.

FAQ structured data once produced prominent answer-box results in search engines. The pattern <script type="application/ld+json">{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"FAQPage","mainEntity":[{"@type":"Question","name":"What is the return policy?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Returns within thirty days, original packaging required."}}]}</script> earned coveted SERP real estate before Google scaled back its FAQ rich-result programme in 2023.

RDFa offers a third in-markup syntax for structured data with explicit vocab declarations. A book listing in RDFa looks like

, and although less commonly used than JSON-LD it remains supported by all major consumers.

Local business markup helps maps and discovery surfaces find a venue. The block <script type="application/ld+json">{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"Restaurant","name":"Hilltop Cafe","address":{"@type":"PostalAddress","streetAddress":"12 Hill Road","addressLocality":"Bristol","postalCode":"BS8 1AB","addressCountry":"GB"},"telephone":"+44 117 555 0123","openingHours":["Mo-Fr 08:00-17:00"]}</script> exposes hours, address, and phone in a single canonical form.

Review and aggregate rating annotations appear extensively across product and service pages. The combination of

participates in rich results while remaining the visible product summary.

Job postings have a dedicated schema vocabulary that aggregators consume directly. The fragment <script type="application/ld+json">{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"JobPosting","title":"Senior Backend Engineer","datePosted":"2025-06-10","validThrough":"2025-07-10T23:59","employmentType":"FULL_TIME","hiringOrganization":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Example Corp"},"baseSalary":{"@type":"MonetaryAmount","currency":"AUD","value":{"@type":"QuantitativeValue","value":170000,"unitText":"YEAR"}}}</script> feeds Indeed, LinkedIn, and Google Jobs.

The element gives a script a bitmap surface to draw on with the 2D context. Markup like Your browser does not support canvas; see the data table. exposes a drawable area while providing accessible fallback content for non-graphical user agents.

High-DPI displays require canvases to be scaled internally to avoid blurry rendering. A pattern pairs CSS-pixel dimensions with bitmap-pixel dimensions: <canvas id="plot" style="width:400px;height:200px" width="800" height="400"></canvas> creates a 400-by-200 visual area backed by an 800-by-400 bitmap, after which ctx.scale(2, 2) means subsequent drawing commands work in CSS pixels.

Image manipulation through canvas typically pairs the element with an Image source. Markup like lets a script load the image, draw it with ctx.drawImage, read pixel data with ctx.getImageData, and write modified data back, provided the cross-origin headers permit it.

WebGL contexts are obtained from the same <canvas> element with a different argument to getContext. The element <canvas id="gl" width="1024" height="768" data-mode="webgl2"></canvas> can be used either for 2D rendering or, with canvas.getContext('webgl2'), for hardware-accelerated 3D, although only one context type may be active per canvas in its lifetime.

Offscreen canvas allows rendering to happen in a worker thread without blocking the main UI. A page can declare <canvas id="viz" width="600" height="400"></canvas> and then call viz.transferControlToOffscreen() to hand the surface to a worker, which performs all drawing operations and posts back when frames are ready, suitable for high-frame-rate visualisations like waveform displays.

Capturing user signatures often uses pointer events on a canvas. The combination <canvas id="signature" width="500" height="200" style="touch-action:none;border:1px solid #999"></canvas><button type="button" id="clear-signature">Clear</button> works on both desktop and tablet because touch-action:none prevents the browser from intercepting drags for scrolling or zooming, leaving them for the script to interpret as ink strokes.

Exporting a canvas as a downloadable image uses the toDataURL or toBlob methods. Combined with markup like Download PNG, a one-line script sets download.href = diagram.toDataURL('image/png') and the standard browser download dialog appears on click without any server roundtrip.

Game loops on canvas typically use requestAnimationFrame to synchronise with the display refresh. Markup like <canvas id="game" width="800" height="600" tabindex="0" aria-label="Game area"></canvas> establishes a focusable canvas that can receive keyboard input directly, while the script's loop calls ctx.clearRect, advances state, and redraws each frame before scheduling the next.

Charts can be rendered on the canvas with carefully chosen pixel-snapping to avoid blurry lines. Markup like wraps the canvas in semantic markup so search engines and screen readers see a labelled figure, and a sparkline routine draws polyline segments anchored to half-pixel coordinates to avoid antialiased smearing.

Canvas accessibility remains a perennial challenge because the bitmap surface has no inherent semantics. Adding accessible content with
User locations
CountryUsers
 provides both the visual surface and an embedded fallback table that screen readers can announce.

Inline SVG is parseable and stylable as part of the host document. A simple icon takes the form <svg width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M5 12l4 4L19 6"/></svg>, where the currentColor keyword inherits the surrounding text colour and aria-hidden removes the decorative shape from the accessibility tree.

SVG sprites avoid loading many separate icon files by collecting reusable shapes into a single hidden block. The pattern <svg style="display:none"><defs><symbol id="icon-cart" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path d="M3 3h2l3 12h12l2-8H7"/></symbol></defs></svg> at the top of the document allows later markup such as <svg class="icon" width="20" height="20"><use href="#icon-cart"/></svg> to render the cached symbol anywhere.

Charts drawn in SVG enjoy crisp scaling and resolution independence. A bar chart skeleton like <svg viewBox="0 0 400 200" role="img" aria-label="Quarterly revenue"><rect x="20" y="100" width="60" height="80" fill="#3b82f6"/><rect x="100" y="60" width="60" height="120" fill="#3b82f6"/><rect x="180" y="40" width="60" height="140" fill="#3b82f6"/></svg> resizes cleanly when its container changes width.

Text inside SVG uses its own typography elements that respect the document's font stack. A label might be rendered as <svg viewBox="0 0 200 60" font-family="system-ui" font-size="16"><text x="10" y="35" fill="#111">Total: $1,240</text></svg>, with the font specified on the root SVG element and inherited by descendant text unless overridden locally.

SVG path data uses a compact mini-language of commands. The element <svg viewBox="0 0 100 100"><path d="M50 10 L90 90 L10 90 Z" fill="#fbbf24" stroke="#92400e" stroke-width="2"/></svg> draws a triangle by moving to (50,10), drawing lines to (90,90) and (10,90), and closing back to the start with the Z command.

Animations on SVG attributes can be expressed declaratively with SMIL elements. A pulsing dot reads <svg width="40" height="40" viewBox="0 0 40 40"><circle cx="20" cy="20" r="6" fill="#10b981"><animate attributeName="r" values="6;12;6" dur="1.5s" repeatCount="indefinite"/></circle></svg>, animating the radius without CSS or JavaScript, although CSS animations are preferred in most modern code.

Logos and brand marks often live as inline SVG so they pick up CSS styles and dark-mode variations. The pattern renders the wordmark in the current colour and supplies an accessible name through the child.

Gradients in SVG are defined once and referenced by URL. The pattern <svg viewBox="0 0 200 100"><defs><linearGradient id="sky" x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="1"><stop offset="0%" stop-color="#1e3a8a"/><stop offset="100%" stop-color="#93c5fd"/></linearGradient></defs><rect x="0" y="0" width="200" height="100" fill="url(#sky)"/></svg> fills a rectangle with a vertical gradient.

Clipping paths confine SVG content to an arbitrary shape. The pattern <svg viewBox="0 0 100 100"><defs><clipPath id="circle-clip"><circle cx="50" cy="50" r="45"/></clipPath></defs><image href="avatar.jpg" x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" clip-path="url(#circle-clip)" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/></svg> displays a circular avatar without the additional masking layers a CSS-only approach would require.

SVG can host interactive widgets when paired with link elements and pointer handlers. A simple selectable map of provinces reads , with each region wrapped in an giving keyboard activation and a tooltip via the nested title.

The native element provides modal and non-modal dialogs without bespoke focus-trapping code. Markup like

Permanently delete this file?

 shows a modal when opened with showModal(), and form method="dialog" closes it returning the chosen button's value.

The ::backdrop pseudo-element styles the area behind an open modal dialog. A stylesheet rule like dialog::backdrop { background: rgba(15, 23, 42, 0.7); backdrop-filter: blur(6px); } combined with markup such as

Account settings

 produces a dimmed and blurred background without any additional overlay element.

The popover API renders non-modal panels that close on outside click and escape. A menu reads

Keyboard shortcuts

Ctrl-K to open command palette

, with the browser handling top-layer rendering and dismissal without JavaScript.

Disclosure widgets that group several details elements form an accordion. The pattern
How do refunds work?

Refunds are processed within seven business days.

Where do you ship?

We ship to Australia, New Zealand, and the United Kingdom.

ties the panels together by name so opening one closes the others.

Confirmation dialogs that return a value are clean to write with method="dialog". The form <dialog id="choose-color"><form method="dialog"><label><input type="radio" name="color" value="red" checked>Red</label><label><input type="radio" name="color" value="green">Green</label><button value="ok">OK</button><button value="cancel">Cancel</button></form></dialog> exposes the dialog.returnValue after submission for the calling script to consume.

Sheet-style bottom dialogs on mobile can be styled with CSS without changing the underlying markup. A dialog declared as

Share

Pick a destination

 can be styled with @media (max-width: 640px) { .sheet { margin: auto auto 0; max-width: 100%; border-radius: 12px 12px 0 0 } } so on phones the same element animates up from the bottom of the screen.

Nested disclosure regions can describe optional advanced settings without overwhelming the default view. Markup like <details><summary>Advanced</summary><label>Timeout (ms)<input type="number" name="timeout" min="100" max="60000" value="5000"></label><details><summary>Even more advanced</summary><label>Retry strategy<select name="retry"><option>exponential</option><option>fixed</option></select></label></details></details> creates a hierarchical settings panel.

The hidden attribute and the [hidden] selector still have a place alongside dialog and popover. A toast region might be marked
Saved
, with the script removing the hidden attribute when a save succeeds and reapplying it after a timeout. Unlike popover, hidden has no special focus or top-layer semantics.

The inert attribute removes a subtree from focus and assistive-technology consideration while leaving it visible. Marking the rest of the page with <main inert>...</main> while a modal is open prevents tab order from leaking out of the dialog, an effect that previously required extensive ARIA and tabindex manipulation.

Tooltip patterns can use popover with anchor positioning emerging in modern browsers. The pattern
Press Ctrl-K to search
lets the browser place and dismiss the tip without a custom positioning engine.

The native <video> element accepts multiple <source> children so the browser can pick a format it supports. Markup like <video controls width="640" preload="metadata" poster="thumb.jpg"><source src="talk.av1.mp4" type="video/mp4; codecs=av01.0.05M.08"><source src="talk.h264.mp4" type="video/mp4; codecs=avc1.640028"><track kind="captions" srclang="en" src="talk.en.vtt" label="English" default></video> falls back from AV1 to H.264 and ships English captions.

Autoplay is permitted only when the video is muted in most browsers. The pattern <video autoplay muted loop playsinline width="100%" aria-label="Promotional background"><source src="bg.mp4" type="video/mp4"></video> is the standard way to ship a decorative looping background, with playsinline ensuring that iOS does not automatically expand the playback to fullscreen.

Podcast pages frequently embed the show audio alongside chapter markers. A typical block is
Chapters
  1. 00:00 Introduction
  2. 04:32 Listener questions
  3. 22:11 Main topic
, with preload="none" so a large file does not begin downloading until the user activates playback.

Adaptive streaming through HLS or DASH usually requires a manifest URL rather than a static file. A modern setup is <video controls width="100%" data-src="https://cdn.example.org/live/manifest.m3u8"></video> paired with the hls.js library, which attaches to the element if the browser does not have native HLS, while Safari plays the manifest directly without any helper.

The <track> element layers captions, subtitles, descriptions, and chapters onto a video. A bilingual classroom video might carry <video controls src="lesson.mp4"><track kind="captions" srclang="en" src="lesson.en.vtt" label="English" default><track kind="subtitles" srclang="fr" src="lesson.fr.vtt" label="Français"><track kind="descriptions" srclang="en" src="lesson.ad.vtt" label="Audio descriptions"></video> for a fully accessible delivery.

Picture-in-picture is offered by browsers as a built-in capability that the user invokes. The basic markup <video id="clip" src="clip.mp4" controls width="480"></video><button onclick="clip.requestPictureInPicture()">Pop out</button> hands a small floating window to the user that survives tab switches, with the disablepictureinpicture attribute available when the behaviour is not desired.

Synchronised lyric or transcript displays often combine the audio element with a custom timeline. A page might use
  1. First line
  2. Second line
  3. Third line
and a script that listens for timeupdate events to highlight the current line.

Background music with a user-selectable mute button needs careful pairing. The pattern <audio id="bg" src="ambient.ogg" loop autoplay muted></audio><button type="button" id="sound-toggle" aria-pressed="true">Sound off</button> shows the button in its default muted state, and the toggle script flips the aria-pressed value and the element's muted property together.

Live streaming for events often pairs a video element with chat. A two-pane layout like <section class="stream"><video id="live" controls autoplay muted playsinline poster="stream-poster.jpg"><source src="https://cdn.example.org/live.m3u8" type="application/vnd.apple.mpegurl"></video><aside id="chat" aria-label="Live chat"></aside></section> establishes the structural skeleton before any framework hydration.

MediaSession metadata lets the browser show rich now-playing information in the operating system. A page playing audio uses <audio id="player" controls src="podcast.mp3"></audio> together with navigator.mediaSession.metadata = new MediaMetadata({ title: 'Episode 47', artist: 'Show name', album: 'Season 3', artwork: [{ src: 'cover.jpg', sizes: '512x512', type: 'image/jpeg' }] }) so the lock screen displays the cover and title.

HTML email rendering across clients still depends substantially on tables for layout because flexbox and grid are unsupported in many older email engines. A common pattern is
Header
, with role="presentation" suppressing screen-reader table semantics.
Inline styles are mandatory in HTML email because many clients strip
Outlook on Windows uses Microsoft Word as its rendering engine, which forces idiosyncratic markup. A bulletproof button uses conditional comments such as Continue.
Images in email need explicit dimensions and a meaningful alt text because images are often blocked by default. The pattern avoids the broken-layout effect that occurs when images fail to load.

Web fonts in email are unreliable; Gmail strips most @font-face declarations. A common defensive pattern is to attach an inline style to every text-bearing element, for example Hello there, since email engines do not always inherit fonts down through nested tables the way browsers cascade fonts through normal HTML.

Plain-text equivalents accompany every multipart email and a useful pattern is to mirror the visual hierarchy through hidden preview text near the top of the HTML body. The snippet
Confirm your subscription before midnight to receive 20% off your first order.
populates the inbox preview line on most clients.

Background colours need to be set on multiple nesting levels because some email clients only honour them on table cells, not on the body. A defensive pattern starts with
...
to set the colour with bgcolor and inline style on every container.

Dark-mode handling in email uses the prefers-color-scheme media query but with caveats. A safe inversion is <style>@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { .container { background:#0f172a !important; color:#e2e8f0 !important } .logo-light { display:none !important } .logo-dark { display:block !important } }</style> attached to dark-mode-aware classes on a <td class="container">.

Unsubscribe and CAN-SPAM compliance details are usually placed in a small footer table. A typical block is
You're receiving this because you signed up at example.com.
Unsubscribe · 1 Acme Way, Sydney NSW 2000
.

Spacer cells using empty s with explicit heights are an enduring email pattern. The fragment   creates vertical whitespace that Outlook for Windows respects, where margin and padding on text elements are often collapsed or ignored, and the line-height and font-size are set explicitly to defeat the Word-rendering engine's default minimum row height.

Self-hosting a variable font with multiple optical-size axes shrinks the CSS surface considerably. The block

A line of careful sans-serif

renders a single weight from a font file that can supply any weight from 100 to 900.

Preloading the first paint's font avoids the brief invisible-text flash. The combination <link rel="preload" as="font" type="font/woff2" href="/fonts/Inter-Regular.woff2" crossorigin> in the head and a matching @font-face declaration with font-display:swap encourages the browser to fetch the woff2 with high priority and apply it as soon as it arrives.

Google Fonts can be requested with a single stylesheet link with preconnect hints to shave milliseconds off first paint. The pattern <link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com"><link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin><link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter:wght@400;700&display=swap" rel="stylesheet"> requests only the weights actually used.

Local-font fallback hints reduce visible reflow when a remote font arrives. The pattern <style>@font-face{font-family:'Inter';src:local('Inter'),url('/fonts/Inter.woff2') format('woff2');font-display:swap;ascent-override:90%;descent-override:22%;line-gap-override:0%}</style> uses size-adjust descriptors to match the fallback system metric, so the swap moment is imperceptible even on slow connections.

Optical sizing and feature settings on a single typographic style demonstrate how rich modern text rendering can be. The snippet

The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog

enables old-style numerals, the third stylistic set, and automatic optical sizing.

Subsetting fonts to the latin range substantially reduces bytes shipped. A declaration like <style>@font-face{font-family:'Sora';src:url('/fonts/Sora.latin.woff2') format('woff2');unicode-range:U+0000-00FF,U+0131,U+0152-0153,U+02BB-02BC,U+02C6,U+02DA,U+02DC,U+2000-206F,U+2074,U+20AC,U+2122,U+2191,U+2193,U+2212,U+2215,U+FEFF,U+FFFD;font-display:swap}</style> ships only the glyph coverage typical English-language pages will use.

Icon fonts are increasingly replaced by SVG, but where they persist they need explicit accessibility hiding. The pattern Open menu ensures the private-use codepoint is announced as the visually hidden text, not as a glyph the screen reader cannot interpret.

Web-safe fallbacks before a custom font loads keep the layout stable. A defensible stack reads style="font-family:'Inter','Segoe UI','Helvetica Neue',Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif" on the root <body> element, allowing the browser to display content in a familiar system sans-serif until the requested font is available, with size-adjust tuning preventing the swap from shifting text.

Variable fonts allow continuous weight axes within a single file. The element

Italic-feeling oblique at 450 weight

tunes monospace ratio, casual axis, weight, and slant in one declaration, replacing what would have been several separate font files.

Adobe Fonts and similar paid services usually inject their stylesheet via a small loader. The pattern <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://use.typekit.net/abc1def.css"> in the head, with the project tracking only the kit identifier, contrasts with self-hosted fonts that require each <link rel="preload" as="font"> entry to be maintained alongside the @font-face declarations.

sentence: The viewport meta tag is essential for sensible mobile rendering. The line <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover"> in the head tells the browser to use the device's actual pixel width for the layout viewport and to render full-bleed under display notches and rounded corners.

subtopic: viewport, meta tags, and document head
sentence: Open Graph and Twitter Card metadata drive the rich previews shown when a link is shared. A complete set looks like <meta property="og:title" content="Annual Report 2025"><meta property="og:description" content="Financial results and strategic outlook"><meta property="og:image" content="https://example.com/og/annual-2025.png"><meta property="og:url" content="https://example.com/annual"><meta name="twitter:card" content="summary_large_image">.

subtopic: viewport, meta tags, and document head
sentence: Canonical URLs prevent duplicate-content issues across query-string variants. The line <link rel="canonical" href="https://example.com/articles/quantum-monitoring"> in the head consolidates link equity onto a single canonical address even when the visitor arrived via a tracking parameter such as ?utm_source=twitter that the canonical version omits.

subtopic: viewport, meta tags, and document head
sentence: Locale alternates are signalled through hreflang link tags. A multilingual site might publish <link rel="alternate" hreflang="en" href="https://example.com/about"><link rel="alternate" hreflang="fr" href="https://example.com/fr/a-propos"><link rel="alternate" hreflang="ja" href="https://example.com/ja/about"><link rel="alternate" hreflang="x-default" href="https://example.com/about"> so search engines pick the right locale.

subtopic: viewport, meta tags, and document head
sentence: The colour-scheme meta tag declares which themes a page actively supports. The combination <meta name="color-scheme" content="light dark"><meta name="theme-color" media="(prefers-color-scheme: light)" content="#ffffff"><meta name="theme-color" media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" content="#0f172a"> tells the browser to switch form-control rendering and the address-bar tint per scheme.

subtopic: viewport, meta tags, and document head
sentence: The robots and googlebot meta tags govern indexing behaviour at the page level. A staging environment usually carries <meta name="robots" content="noindex, nofollow"> in the head to keep accidental URLs out of search indexes, with the production build switching to <meta name="robots" content="index, follow, max-image-preview:large">.

subtopic: viewport, meta tags, and document head
sentence: Pinned-tab and apple-touch-icon variants supply higher-quality bookmark visuals to specific clients. A reasonably complete kit reads <link rel="icon" href="/favicon.ico" sizes="any"><link rel="icon" href="/icon.svg" type="image/svg+xml"><link rel="apple-touch-icon" href="/apple-touch-icon.png"><link rel="manifest" href="/site.webmanifest"> in the head, covering the desktop tab, the iOS home screen, and the installable web-app manifest.

subtopic: viewport, meta tags, and document head
sentence: Resource hints sculpt the browser's connection setup. The line <link rel="preconnect" href="https://images.example.com" crossorigin><link rel="dns-prefetch" href="https://images.example.com"> in the head warms a TLS connection and resolves DNS before the first image request actually issues, saving roughly a round trip on the critical path.

subtopic: viewport, meta tags, and document head
sentence: Character encoding declarations should appear within the first 1024 bytes of the document. The standard line <meta charset="utf-8"> as the first child of <head> ensures the parser does not misinterpret bytes before the declaration arrives, and combined with <html lang="en"> at the document root it covers both encoding and primary language for assistive tech and search engines.

subtopic: viewport, meta tags, and document head
sentence: Content Security Policy via meta tag is supported as a fallback when no Content-Security-Policy header is available. The line <meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy" content="default-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data: https://images.example.com; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; script-src 'self'"> declares a baseline policy directly in the document head, although the response-header version is strictly preferred.

ES module script tags participate in the modern dependency graph natively. The line <script type="module" src="/app.js"></script> in the head fetches /app.js and then any of its static import targets without a bundler, while the type="module" attribute also defers the script and applies strict-mode semantics to the top level.

Import maps decouple module specifiers from their on-disk paths. A small map declared as <script type="importmap">{"imports":{"react":"https://esm.sh/react@18","react-dom":"https://esm.sh/react-dom@18"}}</script> lets later module scripts use import React from 'react' without bundling, because the browser resolves bare specifiers via the import map.

The defer attribute on a classic script preserves document-order execution after parsing completes. A common pattern is <script defer src="/analytics.js"></script><script defer src="/cookie-banner.js"></script>, where both scripts execute in source order once the parser reaches the closing </body>, avoiding the layout-blocking semantics of an undecorated <script> in the head.

Subresource integrity prevents a CDN-hosted dependency from delivering a tampered file. The pattern <script src="https://cdn.example.com/lib-3.4.0.js" integrity="sha384-Y9w3a7ZP..." crossorigin="anonymous"></script> instructs the browser to verify the hash of the response body against the declared digest before executing it, refusing to run the script if the hash does not match.

Inline scripts that are part of a hardened Content Security Policy need a nonce. The pair <meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy" content="script-src 'self' 'nonce-r4nd0m';"> in the head and <script nonce="r4nd0m">window.config = { build: 'prod' };</script> permits a single trusted inline block while still rejecting injected scripts that arrive without a matching nonce.

Module workers permit a single source-of-truth for code shared between the main thread and a Web Worker. The combination <script type="module" src="/main.js"></script> on the page and new Worker('/worker.js', { type: 'module' }) inside main.js lets both contexts import from a shared utilities module without duplicating the build output.

Inline data passed from the server to the client can use <script type="application/json"> blocks to avoid the XSS risk of injecting JSON into JavaScript context. The pattern <script type="application/json" id="preload-state">{"user":{"name":"Asha"},"flags":{"beta":true}}</script> followed by JSON.parse(document.getElementById('preload-state').textContent) treats the payload purely as data.

The async attribute on script tags decouples download from execution order, useful for analytics and other independent scripts. The pattern <script async src="https://plausible.io/js/script.js" data-domain="example.com"></script> in the head allows the analytics script to execute as soon as it arrives, regardless of where any preceding script in the document is in its own loading sequence.

Module preloading warms the dependency cache without executing anything yet. The line <link rel="modulepreload" href="/components/checkout.js" crossorigin> hints that the browser should fetch and parse the module ahead of the actual import statement, useful when a route transition is likely to require the bundle within seconds and the user has not yet activated the trigger.

Polyfill loading patterns historically used the nomodule attribute to feed legacy browsers a fallback. The pair <script type="module" src="/app.modern.js"></script><script nomodule src="/app.legacy.js"></script> sends a small modern bundle to ES-module-aware browsers and a heavier transpiled bundle to older ones in a single declarative arrangement, with each browser executing exactly one of the two.
Art direction across breakpoints is the principal use case for the element. A hero image might switch to a portrait crop on phones using , with the desktop variant as the universal fallback.

Resolution switching uses the x descriptor in srcset to provide higher-density variants. A logo at three densities reads , and the browser picks the right variant based on the device pixel ratio of the display.
Width-descriptor srcset paired with sizes lets the browser pick the smallest source that fills the layout slot. A typical content image reads , leaving format negotiation to the browser.
Modern format negotiation through serves AVIF to capable browsers while falling back through WebP to JPEG. The fragment typically saves 30 to 50 percent of bytes on browsers that accept AVIF.

Dark-mode imagery can switch through the picture element's media attribute. The pattern ensures that a chart drawn for a light background swaps for a contrasting version in dark mode without any JavaScript hook.

Aspect ratio attributes prevent layout shift while images load. Always specifying lets the browser reserve a 3:1 box that the image will later fill, eliminating the jump that occurs when the image arrives and the surrounding content reflows.

Background images can be made responsive through the image-set CSS function. A header rule reading .hero { background-image: image-set('hero-1x.jpg' 1x, 'hero-2x.jpg' 2x); } applied to <section class="hero" aria-label="Hero banner"></section> picks the right density variant for the device's screen without any HTML-level changes when the design later shifts the resolution thresholds.

Decorative images that contribute no content meaning need an explicit empty alt. The pattern tells assistive technologies to skip the image entirely, distinguishing it from a missing alt attribute which would cause some screen readers to read out the filename.

Above-the-fold hero images benefit from fetchpriority hints. The pattern instructs the browser to schedule the resource ahead of equally-prioritised resources in the initial page load, often reducing largest-contentful-paint by a noticeable margin.
Low-quality image placeholders inlined as data URIs avoid empty boxes during loading. A pattern such as shows a neutral aspect-ratio box until JavaScript swaps the real source.

A web app becomes installable when it ships a manifest linked from every page. The combination <link rel="manifest" href="/manifest.webmanifest"> in the head and a manifest body containing {"name":"Notebook","short_name":"Notes","start_url":"/","display":"standalone","theme_color":"#0f172a","background_color":"#ffffff","icons":[{"src":"/icon-192.png","sizes":"192x192","type":"image/png"}]} satisfies the basic install prompt criteria.

Service worker registration boilerplate is usually placed in an inline script that gracefully degrades. The fragment <script>if ('serviceWorker' in navigator) { window.addEventListener('load', () => { navigator.serviceWorker.register('/sw.js', { scope: '/' }); }); }</script> registers the worker once the page has finished its initial load without blocking first paint.

Splash screens on iOS require their own apple-mobile-web-app meta tags rather than reading from the manifest. The block <meta name="apple-mobile-web-app-capable" content="yes"><meta name="apple-mobile-web-app-status-bar-style" content="black-translucent"><meta name="apple-mobile-web-app-title" content="Notes"><link rel="apple-touch-startup-image" href="/splash-2048x2732.png" media="(device-width: 1024px) and (device-height: 1366px)"> covers the launch screen on iPad Pro.

Shortcut menus on installed PWAs are declared in the manifest under shortcuts. The entry "shortcuts":[{"name":"New note","url":"/new","icons":[{"src":"/new-icon.png","sizes":"96x96"}]},{"name":"Today","url":"/today"}] presented in the manifest body is surfaced as the long-press menu on the home-screen icon, and the host markup needs only <link rel="manifest" href="/manifest.webmanifest"> in the document head.

Web share targets register a PWA as a destination for the device's share sheet. The manifest declares share_target with {"action":"/share","method":"POST","enctype":"multipart/form-data","params":{"title":"title","text":"text","url":"url","files":[{"name":"file","accept":["image/*"]}]}}, and the host page accepts the incoming payload with markup such as <form action="/share" method="post" enctype="multipart/form-data"><input type="file" name="file" accept="image/*"><button type="submit">Save</button></form>.

Maskable icons fill the entire icon canvas so the operating system can apply a system-defined mask. Alongside the regular <link rel="icon" href="/icon-512.png" sizes="512x512"> declaration, the manifest entry {"src":"/icon-maskable-512.png","sizes":"512x512","type":"image/png","purpose":"maskable"} ensures that Android's adaptive icon shape, which clips up to twenty percent of the outer pixels, never crops the brand glyph.

Display-mode media queries adjust the layout for installed app contexts. The CSS rule @media (display-mode: standalone) { .install-banner { display: none } .nav { padding-top: env(safe-area-inset-top) } } applied to
Install for offline use
...
hides the installation prompt once the PWA is already installed.

Offline fallback pages need to be precached by the service worker and declared in the manifest. The pairing of a service-worker install handler that calls cache.addAll(['/offline.html','/styles.css','/logo.svg']) with the host markup You are offline gives the installed app a graceful failure mode when the network drops.

Push notifications begin with a permission prompt on a user action. A button declared as <button type="button" id="enable-push" aria-pressed="false">Enable notifications</button> wraps Notification.requestPermission() and then the service-worker registration's pushManager.subscribe(), with the host page only needing the button markup and a small script bound to its click.

The beforeinstallprompt event lets a page provide its own install button rather than relying on the browser's default prompt. The combination <button type="button" id="install" hidden>Install Notebook</button> and a small script that captures the event with let evt; window.addEventListener('beforeinstallprompt', e => { e.preventDefault(); evt = e; document.getElementById('install').hidden = false; }) gives the page full control over install timing.

Opening a link in a new tab safely requires both rel tokens: Partner site. Without rel="noopener" the destination page gains access to window.opener and can navigate the original tab, and noreferrer additionally strips the Referer header.

Download links suggest a filename and bypass in-browser rendering: Download the report. The browser saves the resource under the supplied name rather than navigating to it, and the attribute only takes effect for same-origin URLs.
Protocol-specific anchors hand off to the device's native apps. A contact block renders Email support beside Call us and Text us, each opening the matching handler on a phone.
Sponsored and user-generated links carry rel hints so crawlers treat them correctly. An advertisement uses Featured offer, while a reader comment uses a reader's blog.

In-page navigation uses fragment identifiers that match element ids. A table of contents lists Installation and Configuration, pointing at headings such as

Installation

that the browser scrolls into view.
Pagination relations sit in the head and in the visible controls alike. A page declares and , with the matching footer control being Next page.
An anchor with no href parses but is not a link and is not focusable. The placeholder Coming soon behaves like inline text, whereas Action is a discouraged pattern that a real should replace.
Image links wrap an img inside an anchor, and the alt text becomes the link's accessible name. The pattern gives screen-reader users a meaningful link instead of a bare URL.

Preconnect and preload hints are link elements with a rel value. Combining <link rel="preconnect" href="https://cdn.example.com"> with <link rel="preload" href="/fonts/inter.woff2" as="font" type="font/woff2" crossorigin> warms the connection and fetches the font early.

An anchor can also be a fragment-only target with an empty body. Writing creates a jump destination, although on modern pages adding an id directly to the heading, as in

Overview

, is the cleaner approach.

Reserved characters must be escaped so the parser does not read them as markup. A paragraph might explain inside a <div class="box"> sample that < stands for less-than, > for greater-than, and & for the ampersand, so the <div> shows as text.

Currency and trademark glyphs have named entities. A price line might read €49.99, while a notice uses

Acme® and Wandersoft™ are partners.

, all of which the browser resolves to the corresponding Unicode characters.

A non-breaking space keeps two tokens on the same line. Writing

The launch is set for 9 a.m. on 14 March.

stops a break between number and unit, and 10 × 4 keeps a multiplication expression intact.

Numeric character references reach any code point even without a named entity. An em dash appears as

The verdict—unexpected as it was—stood.

, and the same character can be given in hexadecimal as —, both rendering identically.

Mathematical and arrow symbols are convenient as entities. A note reads

If a ≤ b and b ≤ c then a ≤ c.

, and a callout uses See the appendix → with → producing a rightward arrow.

Typographic quotation marks improve body text. Replacing straight quotes, as in

She called it “a quiet triumph” in her review.

and

It’s the team’s best work.

, yields curly punctuation regardless of the editor used.

Showing code samples on a page means escaping every angle bracket. A block reads 
if (x < 10 && y > 0) { run(); }
, where each <, >, and & ensures the operators display verbatim instead of being parsed.

Bullet and copyright glyphs are common in footers. A page foot renders

© 2024 Example Ltd. • All rights reserved.

, where © produces the circled-C and • supplies the dot separator.

Accented letters can be written as entities for safety in older toolchains. The name

Café owner Björk Åberg signed the lease.

uses é, ö, and Å so the diacritics survive even without a UTF-8 declaration.

Some entities exist purely to control invisible whitespace. The thin space   lets a designer write 1 000 000 for grouped digits, and the zero-width joiner ‍ influences how adjacent emoji or scripts combine.

<dl><dt>Latency</dt><dd>The time between a request being issued and the first byte of the response arriving.</dd><dt>Throughput</dt><dd>The volume of work completed per unit of time.</dd></dl> A description list pairs each term with its explanation in a way an unordered list cannot express.

A single term can carry several definitions through multiple dd elements. <dl><dt>Bank</dt><dd>A financial institution that accepts deposits.</dd><dd>The sloping land alongside a river.</dd></dl> groups both senses under one <dt>, the canonical way to mark a polysemous entry.

Synonymous terms may share one definition. <dl><dt>HTTP</dt><dt>Hypertext Transfer Protocol</dt><dd>The application-layer protocol for transmitting hypermedia documents.</dd></dl> places two <dt> elements before a single <dd> so abbreviation and expansion both resolve to it.

Glossary entries can nest inline markup.
Idempotent
An operation that, applied multiple times, has the same effect as applying it once; see PUT versus POST.
shows emphasis and code spans within a definition.

A description list is the right markup for metadata pairs. <dl class="meta"><dt>Author</dt><dd>Priya Nair</dd><dt>Published</dt><dd><time datetime="2024-02-09">9 February 2024</time></dd><dt>Reading time</dt><dd>6 minutes</dd></dl> presents article metadata with proper term-and-value semantics.

Term-description pairs can be grouped in a wrapper div for styling.
Cache
A store of recently used data kept for fast retrieval.
Eviction
Removing an entry to make room for newer data.
uses div grouping, which the spec permits.

Description lists can present question-and-answer content. <dl><dt>Q: Is the API rate-limited?</dt><dd>A: Yes, sixty requests per minute per key.</dd><dt>Q: How do I rotate a key?</dt><dd>A: Generate a new key and revoke the old one.</dd></dl> uses each <dt> for a question.

An A-to-Z glossary combines headings with description lists.

C

Compiler
A program that translates source code into machine code.
Concurrency
Multiple computations making progress within overlapping periods.
keeps each letter group navigable.

A definition can mark up the defining instance of a term. <dl><dt><dfn>Hydration</dfn></dt><dd>The process by which client-side JavaScript attaches event listeners to server-rendered HTML.</dd></dl> nests a <dfn> inside the <dt> so assistive technology recognises the term.

Glossary descriptions can cross-reference other entries.
Tree
A connected acyclic graph.
Graph
A set of vertices joined by edges.
lets a reader jump between related entries.

An ordered list can begin at an arbitrary number with the start attribute.
  1. Tighten the mounting bolts.
  2. Reconnect the power lead.
  3. Run the self-test.
continues a procedure from step seven when a list is split across pages.

The reversed attribute counts an ordered list downward.
  1. Gold medal performance
  2. Silver medal performance
  3. Bronze medal performance
renders the markers as 3, 2, 1, which suits countdowns and ranked lists shown best-last.

A single list item can override its number with the value attribute.
  1. Preheat the oven.
  2. Bake for forty minutes.
  3. Cool on a rack.
jumps the second item to 5 and the third continues from 6.

The type attribute selects a different marker glyph.
  1. Introduction
  2. Method
  3. Results
labels items with uppercase letters, while type="i" yields lowercase Roman numerals and type="I" yields uppercase ones.

Nested ordered lists produce a multi-level outline.
  1. Planning

    2. Estimate effort
  2. Execution

places a child

Ordered lists are appropriate whenever sequence carries meaning. A recipe uses
  1. Whisk the eggs and sugar until pale.
  2. Fold in the sifted flour.
  3. Pour into the lined tin.
because performing the steps out of order would change the outcome.

Combining start and reversed is well defined.
  1. Tenth place
  2. Ninth place
  3. Eighth place
begins the numbering at 10 and decrements, so the three items are marked 10, 9, 8.

List items may contain block content.

  1. Open the configuration file.

    nano config.yml

  2. Set the host and port values.

places a paragraph and a code block inside a single

A changelog reads naturally as a reversed list with explicit numbers.
  1. Fixed a crash on export.
  2. Added dark mode.
  3. Initial public release.
shows the newest release first.

Custom counter styling does not change document semantics. An
  1. Sign the form
  2. Attach the receipt
  3. Submit by Friday
remains a numbered sequence for assistive technology even if CSS replaces the digits via ::marker.

The pre element preserves whitespace exactly as written, including line breaks and runs of spaces. ASCII art such as 
  /\_/\
 ( o.o )
  > ^ <
survives intact because the browser does not collapse the spacing.

Source code is conventionally wrapped in a code element nested inside pre. 
def greet(name):
    return f"Hello, {name}"
keeps the indentation and lets a highlighter target the language- class.

Inline code spans use code without pre. A sentence reads

Run npm install and then npm run build before deploying.

, where each renders in monospace but stays on the same line as the prose.

Keyboard input is marked with kbd and program output with samp. An instruction reads

Press Ctrl+C to copy, and the terminal prints Copied 3 files.

, distinguishing what the user types from what the machine returns.

Variables in formulae use the var element. A maths note reads

The area is w × h, so for w = 4 and h = 3 the result is 12.

, each italicised to mark a placeholder.

A diff can be presented in a pre block with inline spans for colour. 
- const x = 1;
+ const x = 2;
keeps the leading plus and minus aligned while CSS tints the lines.
