Inside a code block, angle brackets in the sample must still be escaped. 
<button type="submit">Send</button>
displays a snippet of markup as visible text because each < and > prevents the browser from parsing the tags.

Terminal sessions read clearly when prompts and output are styled separately. 
$ git status
On branch main
nothing to commit, working tree clean
uses a span for the shell prompt.

Ruby annotations place a pronunciation gloss above base text. The markup <ruby>東京<rt>とうきょう</rt></ruby> renders the hiragana reading small and centred over the kanji for Tokyo, the standard way furigana is shown.

The rp element supplies fallback parentheses for browsers without ruby support. Writing <ruby>漢<rp>(</rp><rt>かん</rt><rp>)</rp>字<rp>(</rp><rt>じ</rt><rp>)</rp></ruby> degrades gracefully to parenthesised readings when annotation cannot be positioned above.

A whole phrase can take a single ruby annotation. The construction <ruby>今日<rt>きょう</rt></ruby>はよい天気です glosses only the first compound while the rest of the sentence stays as ordinary inline text in the paragraph.

Per-character annotation interleaves base and rt segments. <ruby>北<rt>べい</rt>京<rt>じん</rt></ruby> attaches one reading to each kanji rather than treating the pair as one unit, which is preferred for teaching materials.

Ruby can annotate with translation glosses rather than phonetics. The markup <ruby>電腦<rt lang="en">computer</rt></ruby> places an English equivalent above the Chinese term, a pattern used in bilingual learning resources.

Nested ruby allows two layers of annotation on one base. The form <ruby><ruby>平京<rt>へいけい</rt></ruby><rt>old name of Kyoto</rt></ruby> places a phonetic reading on the inner ruby and an explanatory gloss on the outer one.
A dictionary entry can combine ruby with other inline elements. 桃花とうか introduces the term with its reading, and a following peach blossom supplies the translation.

The lang attribute matters for ruby because Chinese and Japanese share code points but differ in glyphs. Marking <ruby lang="ja">名前<rt>なまえ</rt></ruby> tells the browser to render the base text with the Japanese font.

Ruby text size is controlled with CSS without altering the markup. A rule like ruby rt { font-size: 0.6em } shrinks the gloss in <ruby>勉強<rt>べんきょう</rt></ruby> while leaving the base characters at their normal size.
Ruby works inside headings and links as well as plain prose. A navigation link such as 京都きょうと keeps the furigana visible while the whole compound remains a single clickable target.

The dir attribute sets the base direction of a passage. A snippet of Arabic in an English page uses

مرحبا بالعالم

, which makes the text flow from right to left and align to the right edge.

The bdi element isolates a run of unknown directionality. A username of unpredictable script is shown as

User ليلى posted a comment.

, keeping the English words around it correctly ordered.

The bdo element forcibly overrides text direction. Writing

123 Main Street

displays the characters in reverse order regardless of their inherent directionality, a rarely needed override.

Setting direction at the document root mirrors layout as well as text. A Hebrew site begins with <html lang="he" dir="rtl"> so scrollbars, list markers, and the default float side all move to the opposite edge.

Mixed-direction sentences are common when a Latin term appears in RTL prose. The markup

أستخدم JavaScript في العمل

wraps the English word in an LTR span so it reads correctly.

Form controls inherit direction from the dir attribute. An RTL search box is written <input type="search" dir="rtl" placeholder="ابحث هنا"> so the caret starts on the right and the placeholder aligns to that edge.

The value dir="auto" lets the browser infer direction from the first strong character. A comment field uses <textarea dir="auto"></textarea> so that whether a user types Arabic or English the text aligns sensibly.

Tables flip their column order under RTL. A
الاسمالعمر
سارة30
places the first column on the right to match the surrounding Arabic.

Numbers inside RTL text follow the bidirectional algorithm. The line

السعر هو 99.50 دولار

keeps the digits 99.50 in left-to-right order even though the words around them flow right to left.

Logical CSS properties pair well with bidirectional markup. With a paragraph marked

…

, a rule using margin-inline-start instead of margin-left shifts the spacing to whichever side is the start.

The time element gives a readable date a machine-readable counterpart. Writing

Published 3 November 2024

lets parsers extract the ISO date from the datetime attribute regardless of the visible text.

A time element can encode a precise instant with a time-zone offset. The markup

Doors open at 7:30 pm AEDT

conveys both the wall-clock time and the offset.

Durations are valid datetime values. A recipe states

Bake time: 45 minutes

, where PT45M is the ISO 8601 period syntax that a script can parse into a number of seconds.

A relative phrase can still carry an exact timestamp. A feed item shows

Posted 2 hours ago

, so the friendly text can be recomputed by JavaScript while datetime stays canonical.

Times without dates are permitted. An opening-hours line uses

We open at 9 am and close at 5:30 pm

, each holding a bare clock value.

Year-month and week values are accepted. A report cover reads

Quarter ending June 2024

and a roster references

Shifts for week 32

.

The time element pairs with structured data. An

Concert review

Performed last Saturday

can be complemented by a JSON-LD block whose startDate field repeats the ISO value.

Event listings benefit from time elements on both ends. A card shows

From 15 Jan to 18 Jan

, giving a parser two clean dates to compute the span.

A blog index can mark each entry's date for sorting scripts. The list item
  • Spring update 2 April
    • exposes a sortable value while the label omits the year.

A webinar invite states the offset explicitly. The line

Live session: 2 pm Eastern

lets client scripts convert the moment to the reader's local time accurately.

Tracked changes in prose use the ins and del elements. A revised clause reads

The deadline is Friday Monday.

, where the browser strikes through the deleted word and underlines the inserted one.

Both ins and del accept a datetime attribute recording when the edit happened. The markup

Price: $40 $35

timestamps the revision for an audit trail.

The cite attribute on an edit can point at a document explaining the change. Writing <ins cite="/changelog#v2" datetime="2024-05-10">new clause</ins> links the insertion to the changelog entry that justifies it.

Both ins and del can wrap block-level content, not just inline text. A whole removed paragraph is shown as

This feature has been retired.

, and an inserted list appears inside
  • New option
.

The s element marks content no longer accurate, which differs semantically from del. A shop listing reads

Was $99 Now $59

, where indicates outdated information rather than a tracked editorial deletion.

Wiki-style diffs combine ins and del with CSS for clarity. A revision line is

The committee met on TuesdayWednesday to vote.

, with the class supplying coloured backgrounds beyond the default strike and underline.

Screen readers can be told to announce edits explicitly. Pairing <ins aria-label="inserted text">approved</ins> and <del aria-label="deleted text">pending</del> ensures the change is conveyed even where the visual strike-through is not perceivable.

Legal documents often show amendments inline. A contract clause reads

The tenant shall pay $1,200$1,350 per month.

, preserving the original figure alongside the amended one.

A struck-through term inside an ordered list still keeps its numbering.
  1. Submit the application
  2. Pay the legacy fee
  3. Await confirmation
shows step two as removed while the list markers remain 1, 2, 3.

Combining a timestamp with prose explains an edit history within the document. The line

Revised to clarify scope; the earlier wording was ambiguous.

records both the change and its date.

The mark element highlights text of special relevance to the reader. A search-results snippet renders

The quantum processor reached quantum advantage last year.

, drawing a yellow background behind each matched term.

Marking is semantic, not merely presentational. Writing

Note the warning: do not exceed the rated voltage.

tells assistive technology the phrase is highlighted for attention, distinct from which signals importance.

A quoted passage can mark the part the author wants to draw attention to. The markup

We must act before the end of the quarter or the option lapses.

highlights a phrase inside someone else's words.

The mark element's colour is fully restyleable. A rule like mark { background: #cdeffd; color: inherit } recolours every highlight, so

The clause about indemnity needs review.

appears with a blue wash instead of the default yellow.

Code review tools often mark the lines under discussion. A snippet renders 
const total = price * qty;
, drawing attention to the expression a reviewer has questioned without altering its meaning.

Multiple marks can be styled differently with classes. A study aid writes

The reaction is exothermic and irreversible.

, where .key and .term receive distinct highlight colours.

Marked text can be combined with inline emphasis. The phrase

Remember: save your work before closing the editor.

highlights the run and also marks it as strongly important, two orthogonal meanings stacked.

A glossary preview can mark the term as it appears in context. The card shows

Definition in use: an API exposes functions for other programs to call.

, highlighting the headword inside the example sentence.

Highlighting can survive into print stylesheets. A rule @media print { mark { background: transparent; text-decoration: underline } } turns

The clause on liability is critical.

into an underline on paper where colour is unreliable.

Annotated transcripts mark the speaker's emphasised words. A line reads

Host: And that is exactly the point I was making.

, with the mark preserving the spoken stress in written form.

The meter element represents a scalar value within a known range. A disk gauge renders <meter min="0" max="100" value="73">73% full</meter>, and the browser colours the bar green, yellow, or red depending on the low and high thresholds.

Threshold attributes shape how a meter is coloured. Writing <meter min="0" max="10" low="3" high="7" optimum="9" value="8">8 of 10</meter> tells the browser that higher is better, so a value of 8 lands in the favourable zone.

The progress element shows task completion rather than a static measurement. A determinate bar renders <progress value="0.6" max="1">60%</progress>, and omitting the value attribute, as in <progress></progress>, produces an indeterminate animated bar.

Both meter and progress should carry an accessible label. The pattern <label for="upload">Upload</label><progress id="upload" value="40" max="100"></progress> associates the visible label, while aria-label is an alternative when no visible text exists.

A meter is the right element for a measurement, never for a percentage of an unrelated task. A battery indicator uses <meter min="0" max="100" value="22" low="15">22%</meter>, since the charge level is a genuine measured quantity within a fixed scale.

The fallback text inside a meter shows where the element is unsupported. Browsers that understand <meter value="0.8">strong</meter> draw the gauge, while older agents render the word strong, so the content should be a sensible textual summary.

Progress values update dynamically from JavaScript. Given <progress id="job" value="0" max="100"></progress>, a script assigns document.getElementById('job').value = 75 as work proceeds, and the bar grows without any markup change.

A meter can express a rating out of a maximum. A review widget renders

Score: 4 out of 5

, giving a compact visual gauge alongside the numeric label.
Meters appear naturally inside table cells. A row shows Storage410 GB, embedding a gauge for each resource in a capacity table.

Several meters can be stacked to compare quantities. A dashboard lists
  • CPU 62%
  • RAM 81%
, one gauge per metric.

The output element holds the result of a calculation. A form pairs two number inputs with <output name="sum" for="a b">0</output>, and a small script writes the total into the output whenever either field changes.

An output is implicitly a live region, so screen readers announce updates. The markup <input type="range" id="vol" min="0" max="11"><output for="vol">5</output> means the new value is read aloud as the slider moves.

The for attribute lists the ids of the inputs that feed an output. Writing <output for="price quantity discount">$0.00</output> documents the calculation's dependencies directly in the markup, even though the arithmetic itself lives in script.

A currency converter uses an output for the converted figure. The form shows and

Converts to 0 EUR

, updated on every keystroke.

An output element can be styled like any inline element. A rule output { font-weight: bold; color: #1a7f37 } makes the computed value in

Total: $48.00

stand out from the surrounding label text.

A BMI calculator displays its result in an output. The markup <output name="bmi" for="height weight">--</output> starts with a placeholder and is overwritten when both the height and weight inputs hold valid numbers.

Output works inside a fieldset to scope a calculation. <fieldset><legend>Tip calculator</legend><input type="number" id="bill"><output for="bill">$0.00</output></fieldset> groups the inputs and the live result as one logical unit.

A form's oninput handler is the natural place to refresh an output. With <form oninput="result.value = parseInt(a.value) + parseInt(b.value)"><input id="a" type="number"> + <input id="b" type="number"> = <output id="result">0</output></form>, the sum recomputes automatically.

Multiple outputs in one form report several derived figures. A checkout shows <output id="subtotal">$0</output>, <output id="tax">$0</output>, and <output id="grand">$0</output>, each updated from the same set of quantity inputs.

An output can present a validation summary. The element <output id="status" for="password">Enter a password</output> changes its text to a strength rating as the user types, acting as a live, programmatically associated hint.

A file picker is created with the file input type. The control <input type="file" name="resume" id="resume"> opens the operating system's file dialog, and the chosen filename appears next to the button after selection.

The multiple attribute lets a single control accept several files. Writing <input type="file" name="photos" multiple> allows the user to select an entire batch at once, which the form submits as a list under the same field name.

The accept attribute filters the dialog to particular file types. The control <input type="file" accept=".pdf,.docx"> shows only documents, while <input type="file" accept="image/*"> restricts the picker to image files of any format.

On mobile, the capture attribute requests a camera or microphone directly. The markup <input type="file" accept="image/*" capture="environment"> opens the rear camera so the user photographs a document instead of browsing stored files.

A file input must live inside a form with the right encoding. The element <form action="/upload" method="post" enctype="multipart/form-data"><input type="file" name="doc"><button>Send</button></form> uses multipart encoding so the binary content transmits correctly.

Styling a file input directly is awkward, so a visible label is used as the button. The pattern <label class="upload-btn" for="file">Choose a file</label><input type="file" id="file" hidden> hides the native control and styles the label instead.

A required file input refuses an empty submission. The control <input type="file" name="id-scan" required accept="image/*"> blocks the form until the user picks an image, surfacing a native validation message in the browser's language.

Folder uploads are possible with a non-standard but widely supported attribute. The control <input type="file" webkitdirectory multiple> lets the user select a whole directory, and the browser submits every file inside it with relative paths.

A drop zone pairs a file input with a styled container. The markup

Drag files here or click to browse

gives both drag-and-drop and click-to-select behaviour.

Multiple file inputs can collect distinct documents in one form. A loan application uses <input type="file" name="payslip" accept=".pdf"> and <input type="file" name="bank-statement" accept=".pdf">, each with its own label and required flag.

A multi-line text field is created with the textarea element. The control <textarea name="comment" rows="5" cols="40">Default text</textarea> shows five visible rows and forty columns, with any content between the tags appearing as the initial value.

The maxlength attribute caps how much can be typed into a textarea. Writing <textarea name="bio" maxlength="280" placeholder="Tell us about yourself"></textarea> prevents the field from exceeding 280 characters, mirroring a familiar limit.

The wrap attribute controls how line breaks are submitted. A textarea with <textarea wrap="hard" cols="30"></textarea> inserts real newlines at the wrap points when the form is sent, whereas wrap="soft" submits the text as one unbroken run.

A textarea needs an associated label like any form control. The pattern <label for="feedback">Your feedback</label><textarea id="feedback" name="feedback" required></textarea> ties the label to the field and makes an empty submission fail validation.

Resizing behaviour is governed by CSS, not markup. A rule textarea { resize: vertical } applied to <textarea name="notes"></textarea> lets the user drag the height but not the width, keeping the page layout stable.

A readonly textarea shows content the user can select but not edit. The element <textarea readonly rows="4">Generated API key: 9f3a-7c2e-...</textarea> lets the value be copied while preventing accidental modification.

Whitespace inside the textarea tags is significant. Because <textarea>
Line one
Line two
</textarea> preserves the leading newline, authors write the opening tag and the first line of content together to avoid an unwanted blank line.

An auto-growing comment box pairs a textarea with a script that adjusts its height. The base markup <textarea id="msg" rows="1" placeholder="Write a reply"></textarea> starts at one row and expands as the input handler updates style.height.

A textarea can be tied to a form it does not visually contain. Using <textarea form="survey" name="open-answer"></textarea> with a form whose id is survey submits the field's value even though the textarea sits elsewhere in the document.

Spellcheck and autocapitalisation are controllable attributes. A code-snippet field uses <textarea spellcheck="false" autocapitalize="none" autocorrect="off"></textarea> so the browser does not flag identifiers or capitalise the first letter of each line.

A multi-select list lets the user choose several values at once. The control <select name="toppings" multiple size="5"><option>Mushroom</option><option>Olives</option><option>Onion</option></select> shows five rows and submits every highlighted option.

Options can be pre-selected with the selected attribute. The markup <select name="plan"><option value="free">Free</option><option value="pro" selected>Pro</option></select> opens with Pro chosen so the user sees the default highlighted.

The optgroup element labels a cluster of related options. A country picker uses <select><optgroup label="Europe"><option>France</option><option>Spain</option></optgroup><optgroup label="Asia"><option>Japan</option></optgroup></select> to give the dropdown headings.
An option's submitted value can differ from its visible text. Writing <option value="us">United States</option> sends the short code us to the server while showing the full country name to the user.

A whole optgroup can be disabled at once. The markup <select><optgroup label="Sold out" disabled><option>Large</option><option>Medium</option></optgroup><optgroup label="Available"><option>Small</option></optgroup></select> greys out every option in the first group.

A select still needs a label for accessibility. The pattern <label for="lang">Language</label><select id="lang" name="lang"><option>English</option><option>Spanish</option></select> ties the visible label to the dropdown for screen-reader users.

A leading placeholder option can be both disabled and selected. Writing <select required><option value="" disabled selected>Choose a size</option><option>Small</option><option>Large</option></select> forces a real choice before the form will submit.

Individual options can be disabled while leaving the rest selectable. The control <select name="slot"><option>9:00</option><option disabled>10:00 (full)</option><option>11:00</option></select> shows the unavailable time but blocks its selection.

Options can be styled in supporting browsers with CSS. A rule option:checked { font-weight: bold } applied within <select multiple><option>Draft</option><option>Published</option></select> emphasises whichever entries the user has highlighted.

Optgroups may be nested inside a select alongside ungrouped options. The control <select><option>None</option><optgroup label="Recent"><option>Project Alpha</option><option>Project Beta</option></optgroup></select> mixes a top-level option with a labelled group.

A native date picker is created with the date input type. The control <input type="date" name="dob" min="1900-01-01" max="2010-12-31"> opens a calendar widget and constrains selection to the allowed range.

The time input type collects a clock value. Writing <input type="time" name="start" min="09:00" max="17:00" step="900"> restricts entry to business hours and snaps the value to fifteen-minute increments via the step attribute.

A combined date and time field uses the datetime-local type. The control <input type="datetime-local" name="appointment" value="2024-12-01T14:30"> pre-fills both the date and the time without any time-zone component.

The month input collects a year and month only. Writing <input type="month" name="billing-period" value="2024-07"> presents a picker with no day component, which suits a statement period or an expiry field.
The week input type selects an ISO week number. The control <input type="week" name="sprint" min="2024-W01" max="2024-W52"> lets a planner pick a single week of the year for a sprint or roster.

A date input pairs naturally with a label and a help hint. The pattern <label for="checkin">Check-in date</label><input type="date" id="checkin" aria-describedby="checkin-help"><small id="checkin-help">Stays must start on a weekday.</small> associates all three.

Two date inputs together express a range. A booking form uses <input type="date" name="from" id="from"> and <input type="date" name="to" id="to">, and a small script sets the to field's min attribute to whatever the from field holds.

A required date input rejects an empty submission. The control <input type="date" name="deadline" required> blocks the form until a date is chosen, and the browser surfaces a native validation message in the user's locale.

The step attribute on a time field controls the precision of entry. Writing <input type="time" name="alarm" step="1"> exposes a seconds field, while the default omits seconds and accepts only hours and minutes.

Date inputs submit a fixed ISO format regardless of locale display. Even though <input type="date" name="event"> shows the calendar in the user's regional order, the form always sends the value as a YYYY-MM-DD string.

A slider control is created with the range input type. The element <input type="range" name="brightness" min="0" max="100" value="50" step="5"> renders a draggable track that snaps to multiples of five between zero and one hundred.

A range input can show tick marks by referencing a datalist. The pattern <input type="range" min="0" max="10" list="marks"><datalist id="marks"><option value="0"><option value="5"><option value="10"></datalist> draws snap points along the track.

The color input opens the platform's colour picker. Writing <input type="color" name="theme" value="#2b6cb0"> shows a swatch pre-set to a blue hue, and the form submits a seven-character hex string when the user confirms a choice.

A range slider is best paired with an output that mirrors its value. The markup <label for="qty">Quantity</label><input type="range" id="qty" min="1" max="20"><output for="qty">10</output> gives the user a readable number alongside the track.

A color input feeds a live preview without a page reload. With <input type="color" id="bg" value="#ffffff">, a small handler sets document.body.style.background to the picker's value whenever the user adjusts the swatch.

The range input's thumb and track are styleable with vendor pseudo-elements. A rule input[type=range]::-webkit-slider-thumb { background: #e53e3e } recolours the draggable knob of <input type="range" min="0" max="100">.

Two range inputs can approximate a dual-handle slider. A price filter uses <input type="range" name="min-price" min="0" max="500"> and <input type="range" name="max-price" min="0" max="500">, with script keeping the lower handle below the upper.

A disabled range input shows but cannot be moved. The control <input type="range" min="0" max="100" value="30" disabled> displays a fixed position, useful for presenting a read-only gauge built from a form element.

A color input can be tied to a label and a hint. The pattern <label for="accent">Accent colour</label><input type="color" id="accent" aria-describedby="accent-note"><small id="accent-note">Used for buttons and links.</small> associates all three.

The range input reports both value and percentage to assistive tech. Adding aria-label and a visible <output> to <input type="range" aria-label="Volume" min="0" max="11" value="7"> ensures screen readers announce a meaningful position.
An image map turns regions of a picture into links. The markup makes the lobby rectangle clickable.

An area can be a circle by giving a centre and radius. Writing <area shape="circle" coords="200,150,40" href="/meeting-room" alt="Meeting room"> defines a round hotspot inside the parent <map> element.

Irregular shapes use a polygon of coordinate pairs. The element <area shape="poly" coords="10,10,90,20,70,80,5,60" href="/zone-a" alt="Zone A"> traces a four-point outline that the browser treats as a clickable region.

Every area needs alt text because each one is effectively a link. A map of a country might contain <area shape="rect" coords="40,30,110,95" href="/north" alt="Northern region"> so screen-reader users hear a meaningful destination.

A default area covers any part of the image not claimed by another shape. Adding <area shape="default" href="/overview" alt="Full map"> after the specific hotspots gives the leftover pixels a fallback link.
The usemap attribute on the img links it to a map by name. The pairing with ... connects the picture to its set of area definitions.

Area elements can open links in a new tab like any anchor. Writing <area shape="rect" coords="0,0,80,80" href="https://docs.example.com" target="_blank" rel="noopener" alt="Documentation"> applies the same safety tokens used on ordinary links.
Coordinates in an image map are measured in the image's intrinsic pixels. If is scaled by CSS, the area coords still refer to the original dimensions, so the browser maps clicks proportionally.

A map can hold many hotspots for an interactive infographic. <map name="solar"><area shape="circle" coords="60,60,18" href="/sun" alt="Sun"><area shape="circle" coords="150,60,8" href="/earth" alt="Earth"></map> defines two clickable bodies.
An image map degrades to a plain image where no area matches. The markup stays viewable everywhere.
The base element sets a default URL for every relative link on the page. Placing in the head means a later Intro resolves against the CDN path rather than the document's own location.

A base element can also set a default target for links. Writing <base href="/app/" target="_blank"> makes every relative anchor open in a new tab unless an individual <a> overrides it with its own target attribute.

Only the first base element in a document has any effect. If the head contains <base href="/site-a/"> followed by <base href="/site-b/">, the browser honours /site-a/ and silently ignores the second declaration.

The base element must appear before any element that uses a URL. Putting <base href="/assets/"> ahead of <link rel="stylesheet" href="main.css"> ensures the stylesheet path resolves correctly, since elements above the base ignore it.

A base href affects fragment links too, which can surprise authors. With , an in-page link written as Back to top resolves to /help/#top and navigates away rather than scrolling within the current page.
Email and previewed templates often need an explicit base. Adding lets a relative load correctly even when the document is rendered outside its original directory.

A base element changes how forms resolve their action. With <base href="/api/"> in the head, a form written as <form action="submit" method="post"> posts to /api/submit rather than to a path relative to the page itself.
Setting only a target without an href is valid. The element <base target="_self"> leaves URL resolution untouched but makes every relative link default to opening in the same browsing context.
A single-page app served from a sub-path often relies on a base tag. Declaring lets the router treat Settings and Reports as paths under the dashboard mount point.
Absolute URLs are unaffected by the base element. Even with present, a link such as External still points at the full address because it does not need resolving.

The address element marks up contact information for a page or article. A site footer uses
Written by the editorial team. Reach us at hello@example.com.
to mark the contact block semantically.

An address element is rendered in italics by the user agent by default. The block <address>Example Ltd, 14 King Street, Sydney NSW 2000</address> appears slanted, though a stylesheet rule address { font-style: normal } can undo that.

The address element belongs to its nearest article or body, not to arbitrary postal data. A blog post ends with
Posted by Jo Park
, giving the author contact for that article.

Telephone numbers inside an address become tappable with a tel anchor. The block
Support hotline: 1-800-555-1234
lets a phone start a call straight from the contact section.

An address can hold several lines separated by br elements. Writing
Acme Studios
Level 3, 9 Elm Road
Melbourne VIC 3000
keeps each line of the postal address on its own row within the contact block.

An address element should not contain unrelated content such as publication dates. A clean contact block is
Questions? Email info@example.org or visit our contact page.
.

A contact section can combine an address with a heading. The markup

Get in touch

Reception: 03 9123 4567
pairs a labelled region with semantic contact details.

Social links sit comfortably inside an address element. A footer renders
Follow us: RSS · Email
as the page's contact information.

An address element can be styled into a card. With a rule address.card { font-style: normal; border: 1px solid #ddd; padding: 1rem }, the block
Help desk — help@example.com
becomes a bordered panel.

The address element pairs with a footer to give a site-wide contact point. A page ends with
Example Foundation, PO Box 42, Canberra ACT 2600. contact@example.org
.

A datalist supplies autocomplete suggestions to a free-text input. The pairing <input list="fruits" name="fruit"><datalist id="fruits"><option value="Apple"><option value="Apricot"><option value="Avocado"></datalist> lets the user type or pick.

Unlike a select, a datalist still permits values not in the list. With <input list="cities" name="city"><datalist id="cities"><option value="Perth"><option value="Hobart"></datalist>, a user may accept a suggestion or enter a different city entirely.

Datalist options can show a label alongside the value. Writing <datalist id="codes"><option value="AU" label="Australia"><option value="NZ" label="New Zealand"></datalist> presents friendly text while the input receives the short code.

A datalist works with typed inputs beyond plain text. The control <input type="date" list="holidays"><datalist id="holidays"><option value="2024-12-25"><option value="2025-01-01"></datalist> offers suggested dates within the picker.

A datalist can be attached to a range input to mark notable values. The pairing <input type="range" list="levels" min="0" max="100"><datalist id="levels"><option value="25"><option value="50"><option value="75"></datalist> draws tick marks on the slider.

One datalist may be shared by several inputs. Two fields written as <input list="tags" name="tag1"> and <input list="tags" name="tag2"> both reference the same <datalist id="tags"><option value="urgent"><option value="review"></datalist>.

Datalist options can be generated dynamically from JavaScript. Starting with an empty <datalist id="results"></datalist> bound to <input list="results">, a script appends option elements as a search-as-you-type query returns matches.

A datalist offers suggestions for an email field. The control <input type="email" list="domains" name="email"><datalist id="domains"><option value="user@gmail.com"><option value="user@outlook.com"></datalist> hints at common addresses.

The datalist element itself is not rendered, only its options surface as suggestions. Placing <datalist id="units"><option value="kg"><option value="lb"></datalist> anywhere in the body adds no visible markup until an input references it.

A search box gains recent-query hints through a datalist. The pairing <input type="search" list="recent" placeholder="Search"><datalist id="recent"><option value="invoices"><option value="contacts"></datalist> shows prior searches as the user focuses the field.

The hr element marks a thematic break between sections of prose. A short story shifts scene with

The train pulled away.

Years later, she returned to the same platform.

, the rule signalling the gap in time.

An hr is a void element with no closing tag and no content. It is written simply as <hr> between two blocks, and although it renders as a line, its meaning is a topic shift rather than mere decoration.

The hr element is fully restyleable with CSS. A rule hr { border: 0; height: 2px; background: linear-gradient(to right, transparent, #888, transparent) } turns a plain <hr> into a soft tapered divider.

An hr can separate distinct articles on an index page. A feed renders

First post

...

Second post

...

, the rule marking the boundary between entries.

A decorative hr can be replaced with a symbol using a pseudo-element. With hr { border: 0; text-align: center } and hr::after { content: '\2766' }, the <hr> in the document renders as a centred floral glyph instead of a line.

An hr inside a menu separates groups of choices. A context menu lists
  • Cut
  • Copy
  • Paste
    • , the rule dividing the clipboard-read actions from the clipboard-write one.

The hr should not be used purely to draw a line where a CSS border would do. A genuine use is

End of the introduction.

The main argument begins.

, marking a real shift in subject.

An hr is announced by screen readers as a separator. Placing
between

Terms and conditions

and

Privacy policy

conveys to assistive technology that the two passages are distinct topics, not one continuous block.
Margins on an hr control the breathing room around a break. A rule hr { margin: 3rem 0 } applied to the <hr> elements in a long article gives each thematic break generous vertical space.

An hr can carry a class for context-specific styling. The markup <hr class="chapter-break"> paired with hr.chapter-break { width: 40%; margin-inline: auto } produces a short centred divider used only between chapters.

A long quotation is marked with the blockquote element. The passage

We choose to do these things not because they are easy, but because they are hard.

sets the text apart as quoted material.

Short inline quotations use the q element, which adds quotation marks automatically. A sentence reads

She described the result as better than anyone expected at the briefing.

, with the browser supplying locale-appropriate quote glyphs.

The cite element marks the title of a referenced work. A book review writes

The argument in Thinking, Fast and Slow is developed over forty chapters.

, and the user agent italicises the title.

A blockquote is often followed by attribution outside the quote itself. The pattern

Simplicity is the ultimate sophistication.

— Leonardo da Vinci

keeps the source out of the quoted text.

Nested q elements produce nested quotation marks. The sentence

He said, the manager told me finish by Friday and left.

renders the inner quote with a different mark than the outer one in most browsers.
A figure can present a quotation with its caption as attribution. The markup pairs the quote with a semantic caption.

The cite attribute on q and blockquote is for machine consumption, not display. Writing <q cite="https://example.org/report">growth slowed in the second quarter</q> stores the source URL without rendering it on the page.

A pull quote can be styled distinctly from an ordinary blockquote. With a rule blockquote.pull { font-size: 1.5rem; border-left: 4px solid #333; padding-left: 1rem }, the markup

This changes everything.

stands out.

The q element should not be used where literal quotation marks are typed manually. Correct usage is

The sign read mind the gap in bold letters.

, letting the browser, not the author, insert the quote glyphs.

A blockquote can hold multiple paragraphs of quoted prose. The structure

First, we considered the petition.

Then we resolved to act.

keeps two paragraphs inside one quotation.

The sub element lowers text for chemical formulae. A line reads

Water is written H2O and carbon dioxide is CO2.

, with the digits dropped below the baseline to denote atom counts.

The sup element raises text for exponents. A maths note writes

The area of the square is x2 and the volume of the cube is x3.

, lifting the power above the baseline.

Ordinal indicators commonly use sup. A sentence reads

The event is held on the 21st and again on the 3rd of next month.

, raising the letter suffix after each number.

Footnote references are typically marked with sup and an anchor. The text

The figure has since been revised1.

lifts a clickable reference number above the line.

Trademark and degree symbols can be built with sup. A product line reads

The AcmeTM kettle holds 1.7 litres.

, raising the letters, although a dedicated entity like ™ is usually preferable.

Isotopes combine sub and sup on the same symbol. The notation

The isotope is written 146C in the textbook.

places the mass number above and the atomic number below the element letter.

Subscript and superscript are semantic, not just typographic. The markup

The series sum is a1 + a2 + an.

conveys index notation that assistive technology and search can interpret.

Default sub and sup styling can be adjusted with CSS to avoid line-height jumps. A rule sub, sup { line-height: 0 } applied to

E = mc2 remains the famous equation.

keeps the surrounding leading even.

Chemical equations mix both elements freely. A reaction line reads

2H2 + O2 → 2H2O

, with each subscript denoting the atom count in the molecule.

A citation style can render reference markers as raised numbers. The sentence

Recent work confirms the trend3,4 across all regions.

uses sup to lift a comma-separated list of source numbers.

subtopic: line breaks and word break opportunities
sentence:
The br element forces a line break within a block. A poem stanza is written

The woods are lovely, dark and deep,
But I have promises to keep.

, keeping the two lines together in one paragraph.

subtopic: line breaks and word break opportunities
sentence: The wbr element marks an optional break point in a long string. A URL printed as https://example.com/very/long/path/segment wraps cleanly at those marks instead of overflowing the container.

subtopic: line breaks and word break opportunities
sentence:
A br is a void element used for genuine line breaks, not for spacing. Postal addresses are a valid case:

Acme Ltd
14 King Street
Sydney NSW 2000

places each line on its own row.

subtopic: line breaks and word break opportunities
sentence: The wbr element produces no visible character; it only suggests where a break may occur. A long identifier shown as getUserProfileSettings can wrap mid-word without a hyphen appearing.

subtopic: line breaks and word break opportunities
sentence:
Stacking many br elements to create vertical space is poor practice. Instead of

Title


Subtitle

, a margin in CSS should provide the gap, reserving
for breaks that are part of the content.

subtopic: line breaks and word break opportunities
sentence:
Song lyrics are a textbook use of br. A verse is written

Twinkle, twinkle, little star,
How I wonder what you are.

, where the break is meaningful to the text rather than presentational.

subtopic: line breaks and word break opportunities
sentence: The wbr element helps long email addresses wrap inside narrow columns. Writing first.last@subdomain.example.com gives the browser permission to break the address at sensible points.

subtopic: line breaks and word break opportunities
sentence:
A br inside a heading keeps a title on two controlled lines. The markup

The Complete Guide
to Modern Layout

splits the title exactly where the designer intends regardless of viewport width.

subtopic: line breaks and word break opportunities
sentence: The wbr element differs from a soft hyphen, which inserts a visible hyphen on break. A part number shown as ABC123XYZ wraps with no extra character, unlike text containing ­ entities.

subtopic: line breaks and word break opportunities
sentence:
A br is announced as a pause by some screen readers. In a multi-line caption

Figure 2
Annual rainfall by month

, the break separates the figure label from its description for both sighted and assistive-tech users.

The small element marks side comments and fine print. A footer line reads

Prices include GST. Offer valid until stocks last.

, and the user agent renders the text at a reduced size.

Copyright notices are a classic use of small. A page foot shows <footer><small>© 2024 Example Ltd. All rights reserved.</small></footer>, treating the notice as legally required fine print rather than body content.

The small element conveys semantics, not just a smaller font. A product card reads

$49.00 plus shipping

, marking the second phrase as a parenthetical qualification of the price.

Disclaimers attached to a claim use small. An advertisement states

Lose weight fast Results vary; not a substitute for medical advice.

, keeping the caveat tied to the headline.

The small element can be restyled while keeping its meaning. A rule small { font-size: 0.85em; color: #666 } applied to

Last updated yesterday

sets the fine print in muted grey.

Attribution lines often sit in a small element. An image credit reads <figcaption><small>Photograph by Dana Reyes, used under CC BY 4.0</small></figcaption>, marking the credit as a side note to the figure.

Terms-of-use summaries appear as small print under forms. A signup form ends with

By creating an account you agree to our Terms and Privacy Policy.

.

The small element should wrap only short runs, not whole paragraphs of body text. A correct use is

Free trial available (credit card required) for new customers..

Legal small print can be combined with strong for emphasis. A warranty note reads

This warranty does not cover accidental damage.

, keeping the whole run as fine print while stressing one phrase.

A small element nested in a heading marks a subordinate byline. The markup

Annual Report Financial Year 2024

renders the year at a reduced size as a side comment to the main title.

A dedicated search landmark groups a site's search controls. The markup <search><form action="/results" role="search"><input type="search" name="q" aria-label="Search site"><button>Go</button></form></search> exposes the region to assistive technology.

The search input type behaves like text but adds a clear control in some browsers. The element <input type="search" name="query" placeholder="Search products" autocomplete="off"> shows a small cross to empty the field quickly.

A search form should submit with the GET method so the query lands in the URL. Writing <form action="/search" method="get"><input type="search" name="q"><button type="submit">Search</button></form> makes results shareable and bookmarkable.

A search input can offer suggestions via a datalist. The pairing <input type="search" name="q" list="suggestions"><datalist id="suggestions"><option value="laptops"><option value="monitors"></datalist> hints at popular queries.

The role="search" attribute marks a form as the site search even without the search element. A header contains <form role="search" action="/find"><label for="s">Search</label><input id="s" type="search" name="s"></form>.

A search field benefits from a visible label or an aria-label. The compact pattern <input type="search" name="q" aria-label="Search the documentation" placeholder="Search docs"> stays accessible even when no text label is shown.

A search input can be wired to submit on the Enter key alone. The minimal form <form action="/search" method="get"><input type="search" name="q" required></form> needs no button, since pressing Enter inside the field submits it.

An advanced search form combines a search input with filters. The markup <form role="search"><input type="search" name="q"><select name="category"><option>All</option><option>Books</option></select><button>Search</button></form> scopes results.

A search input can preserve the current query as its value. After a search, the field renders as <input type="search" name="q" value="wireless headphones"> so the user sees and can edit the term that produced the results.

A search form can target a specific results pane with formtarget. The button <button type="submit" formtarget="results-frame">Search</button> inside a search form sends the query to an iframe named results-frame instead of the whole page.

A button's type attribute decides what it does. <button type="submit">Save</button> sends the form, <button type="reset">Clear</button> restores defaults, and <button type="button">Preview</button> does nothing until script binds an action.

A button with no type defaults to submit inside a form, which often surprises authors. Writing <button>Toggle</button> inside <form> will submit the form on click, so a non-submitting control must be declared <button type="button">Toggle</button>.

A submit button can carry its own name and value. The control <button type="submit" name="action" value="publish">Publish</button> adds action=publish to the submitted data, letting the server tell which button was pressed.

The formaction attribute lets one form post to different endpoints. A form holds <button type="submit" formaction="/draft">Save draft</button> and <button type="submit" formaction="/publish">Publish</button> side by side.

A button can submit a form it is not nested inside. Using <button type="submit" form="signup">Create account</button> with a form whose id is signup ties the control to that form from elsewhere in the document.

The formmethod attribute can override a form's method per button. A search form set to GET may still include <button type="submit" formmethod="post" formaction="/log">Report</button> to send that one action as a POST request.

A disabled button cannot be clicked or submitted. The control <button type="submit" disabled>Continue</button> is greyed out, and a script removes the disabled attribute once all required fields validate.
A button element can contain rich markup, unlike an input button. The control holds an icon and text.

The formnovalidate attribute lets a submit button skip validation. A form includes <button type="submit" formnovalidate>Save and finish later</button> so a partial draft can be submitted without satisfying every required field.

A reset button restores every control to its initial value. The control <button type="reset">Start over</button> inside a long form returns each input to the value present when the page loaded, with no server round-trip.

A checkbox captures an independent boolean. The pairing <input type="checkbox" id="news" name="subscribe" value="yes"><label for="news">Send me the newsletter</label> ties the box to its label and submits only when ticked.

Radio buttons in a group share one name so only one can be chosen. The set <input type="radio" name="size" value="s" id="s"><label for="s">Small</label><input type="radio" name="size" value="l" id="l"><label for="l">Large</label> is mutually exclusive.

A pre-ticked checkbox uses the checked attribute. Writing <input type="checkbox" name="terms" checked> opens the form with the box already selected, which is appropriate only for genuinely sensible defaults.

Related radio buttons belong inside a fieldset with a legend. The structure <fieldset><legend>Delivery speed</legend><label><input type="radio" name="speed" value="std">Standard</label><label><input type="radio" name="speed" value="exp">Express</label></fieldset> gives the group a heading.

Several checkboxes capturing independent options use distinct names. A preferences form has <input type="checkbox" name="email-alerts"> and <input type="checkbox" name="sms-alerts">, each submitting its own value because the choices are not exclusive.

A checkbox can be wrapped inside its label, removing the need for matching ids. The pattern <label><input type="checkbox" name="agree"> I accept the terms</label> keeps the control and its text associated implicitly.

A required radio group forces a selection before submission. Marking one button in the group, as in <input type="radio" name="plan" value="basic" required>, makes the browser block the form until any option in that named set is chosen.

An indeterminate checkbox is set only from script. Starting with <input type="checkbox" id="select-all">, a handler assigns document.getElementById('select-all').indeterminate = true to show the dash state when child boxes are partly ticked.

A disabled checkbox shows but cannot be toggled. The control <input type="checkbox" name="premium" disabled><label>Premium feature (upgrade required)</label> communicates that the option exists but is unavailable on the current plan.

Custom-styled checkboxes hide the native box and style the label. The pattern <input type="checkbox" id="opt" class="visually-hidden"><label for="opt">Enable notifications</label> lets CSS draw a custom indicator while keeping the real control accessible.
A favicon is declared with a link element in the head. The tag <link rel="icon" href="/favicon.ico" sizes="any"> tells the browser which image to show in the tab and the bookmark list.

Modern sites supply an SVG favicon for crisp scaling. Adding <link rel="icon" type="image/svg+xml" href="/icon.svg"> alongside a fallback <link rel="icon" href="/favicon.ico"> covers both vector-capable and legacy browsers.

Apple devices use a separate touch icon link. The tag <link rel="apple-touch-icon" sizes="180x180" href="/apple-touch-icon.png"> provides the image shown when a user adds the site to their iOS home screen.

Multiple icon links can offer different sizes. A head may list <link rel="icon" sizes="16x16" href="/icon-16.png"> and <link rel="icon" sizes="32x32" href="/icon-32.png">, letting the browser pick the resolution it needs.

A favicon can adapt to dark mode with a media attribute. Declaring <link rel="icon" href="/icon-light.svg" media="(prefers-color-scheme: light)"> and a matching dark variant lets the tab icon match the user's theme.

The mask icon link supplies a monochrome Safari pinned-tab graphic. The tag <link rel="mask-icon" href="/safari-pinned-tab.svg" color="#2b6cb0"> gives a single-colour SVG that Safari tints with the supplied colour.

A web app manifest can also reference icons, but the link tag remains for the tab. A head typically has both <link rel="manifest" href="/site.webmanifest"> and <link rel="icon" href="/favicon.ico"> serving different surfaces.

Without an explicit icon link the browser still requests /favicon.ico by convention. Declaring <link rel="icon" href="/assets/brand/favicon.ico"> lets the file live anywhere rather than only at the site root.

A shortcut icon link is an older syntax kept for compatibility. Some pages still write <link rel="shortcut icon" href="/favicon.ico">, though the modern <link rel="icon"> form alone is sufficient for current browsers.
PNG favicons avoid the legacy ICO container. A head can declare <link rel="icon" type="image/png" sizes="96x96" href="/favicon-96.png"> so the browser loads a plain PNG at a defined size for the tab.
